causal_trace.summary: An authenticated HTTP client controls the opt field accepted by POST /calc after self-registration and session establishment.

The handler starts Node with a fixed --allow-fs-read=/app/* permission scope, but its opt validation accepts strings matching a broad --[A-Za-z|,|\/|\*|\=|\-]+ pattern and rejects only listed exact options. An additional --allow-fs-read= value is not among the listed blocked exact options and is appended to Node arguments.

The spawned evaluator base64-decodes the final argument, tests it against a RegExp loaded from config, and invokes JavaScript eval(expr) when the expression does not match. The supplied bundle does not contain config, so reaching eval with a particular expression remains conditional on regex evasion.

If an attacker supplies an accepted additional filesystem-read permission and an expression that reaches eval, evaluated JavaScript runs in the spawned Node process with the expanded read scope. The container places flag.txt at /flag.txt while the original Node scope is /app/*, and /calc returns the child stdout to the HTTP client.

failure.operation: Conditional JavaScript eval in a Node child process after attacker-controlled permission-option injection

primary_invariant.statement: The child Node process should retain the server-selected filesystem-read scope of /app/* and should not receive attacker-controlled permission flags.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The opt field is forwarded as a Node CLI argument under a syntactic filter and finite exact denylist; this admits an additional --allow-fs-read= option that can alter the child permission scope.

quality.review_notes: Primary source establishes the argument-forwarding and conditional eval paths. No config artifact is supplied, so regex evasion and a complete expression cannot be verified. No exploit transcript, execution result, test, organizer provenance, or remediation patch is present; the stated remediation is source-derived inference rather than patch-backed evidence.

remediation.invariant_restored: The child process receives no client-selected permission flags, so its filesystem-read scope remains the fixed /app/* scope selected by the server.
mitigation_classes: Do not forward attacker-controlled Node CLI options
Use a small explicit allowlist of non-permission options if options are required
Keep the child Node filesystem-read permission scope server-defined
